parts.title: Section 1
parts.passageHtml:
{[A.][331661]} {[At the very beginning of the 20th century, the American grocery stores offered comprehensive services: the customers would ask help from the people behind the counters (called clerks) for the items they liked, and then the clerks would wrap the items up.][331662]} {[For the purpose of saving time, customers had to ask delivery boys or go in person to send the lists of what they intended to buy to the stores in advance and then went to pay for the goods later.][331707]} {[Generally speaking, these grocery stores sold only one brand for each item.][331747]} {[Such early chain stores as A&P stores, although containing full services, were very time-consuming and inefficient for the purchase.][331760]}

{[B. Bom in Virginia, Clarence Saunders left school at the age of 14 in 1895 to work first as a clerk in a grocery store.][331781]} {[During his working in the store, he found that it was very inefficient for people to buy things there.][331805]} {[Without the assistance of computers at that time, shopping was performed in a quite backward way.][331825]} {[Having noticed that this inconvenient shopping mode could lead to tremendous consumption of time and money, Saunders, with great enthusiasm and innovation, proposed an unprecedented solution—let the consumers do self-service in the process of shopping—which might bring a thorough revolution to the whole industry.][331841]}

{[C. In 1902, Saunders moved to Memphis to put his perspective into practice, that is, to establish a grocery wholesale cooperative.][331888]} {[In his newly designed grocery store, he divided the store into three different areas: ‘A front lobby’ served as an entrance, an exit, as well as the checkouts at the front.][331908]} {[‘A sales department’ was deliberately designed to allow customers to wander around the aisle and select their needed groceries.][331943]} {[In this way, the clerks would not do the unnecessary work but arrange more delicate aisle and shelves to display the goods and enable the customers to browse through all the items.][331963]} {[In the gallery above the sales department, supervisors can monitor the customers without disturbing them.][331996]} {[‘Stockroom’, where large fridges were placed to maintain fresh products, is another section of his grocery store only for the staff to enter.][332012]} {[Also, this new shopping design and layout could accommodate more customers to go shopping simultaneously and even lead to some unimaginable phenomena: impulse buying and later supermarket.][332036]}

{[D. On September 6, 1916, Saunders performed the self-service revolution in the USA by opening the first Piggly Wiggly featured by the turnstile at the entrance store at 79 Jefferson Street in Memphis, Tennessee.][332065]} {[Quite distinct from those in other grocery stores, customers in Piggly Wiggly chose the goods on the shelves and paid the items all by themselves.][332099]} {[Inside the Piggly Wiggly, shoppers were not at the mercy of staff.][332125]} {[They were free to roam the store, check out the products and get what they needed by their own hands.][332138]} {[There, the items were clearly priced, and no one forced customers to buy the things they did not need.][332159]} {[As a matter of fact, the biggest benefit that the Piggly Wiggly brought to customers was the money-saving effect.][332179]} {[Self-service was optimistic for the improvement.][332198]} {[‘It is good for both the consumer and retailer because it cuts costs,’ noted George T. Haley, a professor at the University of New Haven and director of the Centre for International Industry Competitiveness, ‘if you look at the way in which grocery stores (previous to Piggly Wiggly and Alpha Beta) were operated, what you can find is that there are a great number of workers involved, and labour is a major expense.][332205]} {[’ Fortunately, the chain stores such as Piggly Wiggly cut the fat.][332281]}

{[E. Piggly Wiggly and this kind of self-service stores soared at that time.][332294]} {[In the first year, Saunders opened nine branches in Memphis.][332307]} {[Meanwhile, Saunders immediately applied a patent for the self-service concept and began franchising Piggly Wiggly stores.][332318]} {[Thanks to the employment of self-service and franchising, the number of Piggly Wiggly had increased to nearly 1,300 by 1923.][332334]} {[Piggly Wiggly sold $100 million (worth $1.][332355]} {[3 billion today) in groceries, which made it the third-biggest grocery retailer in the nation.][332360]} {[After that, this chain store experienced company listing on the New York Stock Exchange, with the stocks doubling from late 1922 to March 1923.][332376]} {[Saunders contributed significantly to the perfect design and layout of grocery stores.][332397]} {[In order to keep the flow rate smooth, Saunders even invented the turnstile to replace the common entrance mode.][332410]}

{[F. Clarence Saunders died in 1953, leaving abundant legacies mainly symbolised by Piggly Wiggly, the pattern of which spread extensively and lasted permanently.][332431]}

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 1 - 5:

Reading Passage 1 has six paragraphs, A-F. Which paragraph contains the following information?

Write the correct letter, A-F, in boxes 1-5 on your answer sheet. 

NB You may use any letter more than once.

questions.explanationHtml:
C

“layout of Clarence Saunders’ store”: cấu trúc trong cửa hàng của Clarence Saunders

Giải thích: Saunsers chia cửa hàng ra làm 3 khu vực: front lobby, sales department và stockroom

questions.text: A reference to a reduction by chain stores in labour costs
questions.explanationHtml:
D

“a reference to a reduction by chain stores in labour costs”: đề cập đến việc những chuỗi cửa hàng giảm chi phí nhân công

Giải thích: nếu nhìn vào cách những cửa hàng tạp hóa thường vận hành, chúng ta có thể thấy rằng sẽ cần rất nhiều nhân viên (there are a great number of workers involved) và chi phí nhân công rất lớn (labour is a major expense) → những chuỗi cửa hàng như Piggly Wiggly (chain stores such as Piggly Wiggly) cắt giảm được phần chi phí phát sinh này (cut the fat).

questions.text: How Clarence Saunders’ idea had been carried out
questions.explanationHtml:
C

“how Clarence Saunders’ idea had been carried out” cách thực hiện ý tưởng của Clarence Saunders 

Giải thích: Saunders chuyển đến Memphis để thực thi tầm nhìn của ông ấy (put his perspective into practice) thông qua việc thành lập một hợp tác xã bán sỉ (establish a grocery wholesale cooperative)

questions.text: How people used to shop before Clarence Saunders’ stores opened
questions.explanationHtml:
A

“how people used to shop before Clarence Saunders’ stores opened”: cách người ta mua sắm trước khi cửa hàng của Saunder ra đời

Giải thích: trước kia, khách hành phải nhờ nhân viên bán hàng lấy hộ những món cần mua (the items they liked). Để tiết kiệm thời gian thì khách hàng thường gửi list mua sắm trước (send the lists of what they intended to buy to the stores in advance) rồi ghé trả tiền sau (pay for the goods later).

questions.text: A description of economic success brought by Clarence Saunders’s stores
questions.explanationHtml:
E

“a description of economic success brought by Clarence Saunders’s stores”: Mô tả những thành tựu về mặt kinh tế mà những cửa hàng của Saunders mang lại

Giải thích: những cửa hàng Piggly Wiggly phát triển mạnh mẽ vào thời đó (soared at that time) → số lượng cửa hàng tăng lên đến 1300 → giá trị lượng hàng hóa bán được lên đến 100 triệu đô → giá cổ phiếu tăng lên gấp đôi (with the stocks doubling)

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 11 - 13:

Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.
Write the correct letter in boxes 11-13 on your answer sheet.

options.text: He wanted to transfer business to retailing.
He thought this could enable customers’ life to be more convenient.
He wanted to create a new shop by himself.

questions.explanationHtml:
11

C

“Why did Clarence Saunders want to propel the improvement of grocery stores at his age?”: Vì sao Saunders muốn thúc đẩy sự phát triển của cửa hàng tạp hóa ở thời của ông ấy?

Giải thích: Saunders nhận ra cách thức mua hàng rất kém hiệu quả (very inefficient) → lãng phí thời gian, tiền bạc cực nhiều (tremendous consumption of time and money) → Saunders đưa ra giải pháp để khách tự phục vụ → có thể cách mạng hóa triệt để ngành bán lẻ (bring a thorough revolution to the whole industry) → chọn C. He thought this could enable customers’ life to be more convenient (tin rằng điều này có thể khiến cho cuộc sống khách hàng thuận tiện hơn)

12

 

“The Piggly Wiggly store was”: cửa hàng Piggly Wiggly thì …

Giải thích: khách hàng ở Piggly Wiggly tự làm mọi thứ (lấy hàng, trả tiền) - và sự “tự phục vụ” này có tiềm năng phát triển (Self-service was optimistic for the improvement) → chọn B. mainly featured in self-service (có đặc trưng chủ yếu là tự phục vụ)

options.text: a fully automatic store system opened soon near his first store.
his Piggly Wiggly store was very popular at that time.
his name was usually connected with Piggly Wiggly stores.
his name was printed together with that of his famous store.

questions.explanationHtml:
13

C

“Today, the main thing associated with Clarence Saunders is that”: ngày nay, thứ chủ yếu gắn liền với tên tuổi Saunders là…

Giải thích: Saunders tuy đã mất nhưng vẫn để lại nhiều di sản (leaving abundant legacies) và được giữ hồn bởi chuỗi cửa hàng Piggly Wiggly (symbolised by Piggly Wiggly) → chọn C. his name was usually connected with Piggly Wiggly stores (tên ông ấy đi liền với chuỗi cửa hàng Piggly Wiggly)
